title: stream-quorum-commit-and-deferred-kernel-binding-to-improve-cuda-graph-replay-correctness
creator: Maya Chen
description: Investigate and implement a coordination mechanism for multi-stream CUDA Graph capture/replay that reduces transient misbinding of kernels and inconsistent KV-prefill state across concurrent decoders. The goal is to eliminate non-deterministic replay failures observed under heavy co-scheduled prefill+decode traffic without regressing latency SLOs or throughput on 8xA100 dedicated nodes.
motivation: Recent in-prod incidents show sporadic token corruption and replay divergence when multiple streams perform near-simultaneous capture and replay. Root cause signals point to race conditions between capture commit and kernel binding decisions plus stale KV cache snapshots. Existing fixes (serialize-all-captures) are safe but regress GPU utilization and increase tail latency. We need a correctness-first approach that preserves concurrency where possible.
proposal_summary: Implement a stream-quorum-commit protocol with deferred kernel binding: each decode stream performs tentative capture using lightweight, idempotent graph fragments and records a capture-hash/epoch. A quorum (configurable per-node or per-pool) must acknowledge the capture epoch before final kernel binding and commit. Kernel selection is deferred until commit time, at which point a deterministic binding routine chooses kernels based on epoch fingerprint and active hardware topology. A KV-prefill watermark will be advanced only at commit, preventing stale cache reads during replay.
design_decisions: Use an epoched capture-hash (64-bit) to identify capture intents and detect drift without heavy metadata exchange
Defer kernel selection until commit to ensure all streams agree on a binding map; kernels remain referenced by stable IDs during tentative capture
Quorum size defaults to 1 for single-stream pools and 3 for multi-stream high-concurrency pools; configurable via pool policies
Introduce a lightweight commit barrier implemented via shared GPU-visible ring buffer + small host-side atomic to minimize CPU-gpu round trips
Keep tentative captures idempotent: replays before commit are allowed but changes are discarded if the epoch is not committed
Fallback fast-path: if commit latency exceeds threshold, auto-fallback to a conservative serialized capture mode for that pool
implementation_tasks: Add capture-epoch field to graph metadata and compute deterministic capture-hash during tentative capture
Implement deferred_binding layer that records kernel candidates and defers kernelHandle->kernelDevice mapping until commit
Create GPU-visible commit ring buffer and host commit orchestrator that satisfies quorum semantics
Modify KV-prefill logic to tag snapshots with epoch and only promote snapshot to active after commit
Add pool policy knobs for quorum size, commit-timeout-ms, and conservative-fallback toggle
Instrument telemetry: commit_latency_ms, commit_retries, aborted_tentative_captures, kernel_binding_mismatches
Add CI smoke tests for deterministic replay across varying interleavings and stress test for high QPS with synthetic filler workload
Write e2e test that reproduces prior divergence bug and validate fix on 8xA100 and heterogenous 4xA100+2xV100 clusters
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer from incident report no longer fails in 1000 runs of CI stress harness
Commit latency p99 < 10ms for single-stream pools and < 40ms for high-concurrency pools under benchmarked load
No measurable regression in steady-state throughput (<= 5% drop) on dedicated 8xA100 nodes
New telemetry exposes commit path behaviors and alerts when fallback is triggered
Rollout plan validated with canary on 1 production pool and automatic rollback on increase in error-rate
test_plan: Unit tests for epoch/hashing logic, integration tests for deferred-binding state transitions, GPU-backed CI that runs 10k multi-stream decode cycles with random interleaving seeds, and an A/B comparison against current master to quantify throughput and p99-latency. Add fuzz harness that flips kernel selection bits during tentative captures to assert commit agreement.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary on staging cluster with dedicated synthetic workloads (2 days). Stage 2: low-traffic production pool (1 node) for 48 hours with tight monitoring. Stage 3: expand to additional production pools gradually by traffic weight (10%, 30%, 60%). Automatic rollback if error-rate or replay divergence increases by > 10% relative to baseline.
risks_and_mitigation: Increased commit latency under contention -> mitigation: conservative-fallback and tunable quorum thresholds
Complexity of deferred binding increases code surface -> mitigation: isolate in new module with clear invariants and heavy unit testing
Edge-case: hardware topology changes mid-epoch (preemption) -> mitigation: detect topology mismatch at commit and force safe re-capture
Undetected false-positive mismatches due to hashing collisions -> mitigation: use 64-bit hash with additional checksum validation for critical fields
